- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% for 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase early forecast values by 10–25% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00), especially in first 5–7 days; apply exponential decay to forecast values post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts: if forecast > 1.5x recent 7-day average, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Forecasts with sentiment history showing alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67) show persistent lag; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for 1–3 days to correct delay.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underperforms; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 5 days to avoid “dead zone” bias.
